Name: kuairand_fm_validation_baseline
Title: Autonomous Improvement of Long-View Ranking on KuaiRand-Pure
Short Hypothesis: A validation-only autonomous experiment loop can reliably reproduce the organizer FM baseline before attempting controlled ranking improvements.
Related Work: Factorization Machines provide the organizer baseline. AI Scientist-v2 provides staged experiment management and tree search. The initial deployment focuses on a trustworthy connection between them.
Abstract: Build an autonomous research workflow around the organizer-provided KuaiRand-Pure Starter Kit. The first stage must reproduce the fixed Factorization Machine baseline using long_view as the relevance label and validation primary=(GAUC+nDCG@5)/2 as the only node-selection score. The workflow must preserve the official chronological split and evaluator, use no external training dataset, and expose no test feedback during research. Later stages may tune the fixed FM and autonomously explore controlled ranking improvements after the baseline connection is verified. Population-level EDA from the official training split is available as validation context in input/data_analysis/eda_summary.json. Those observations are evidence to inspect rather than prescribed Stage 3 directions: each Agent must decide whether they remain relevant to the current incumbent and may support, revise, or reject them. Any temporal or statistical feature that an Agent chooses must be constructed causally from strictly earlier permitted events only.
Experiments: Execute the supplied editable CandidateModel program directly as the Stage 1 baseline; do not replace it with or invoke the legacy run_fm_experiment.py CLI.
Verify finite predictions, the official validation GAUC and nDCG@5, primary computation, early stopping, checkpoint creation, and protected-file hashes.
Accept Stage 1 only if the supplied program writes working/experiment_data.npy and primary reproduces the published baseline within expected seed variation.
For each Stage 3 slot, inspect the same incumbent and validation-only feedback, then independently choose and implement one coherent hypothesis without a controller-assigned algorithm direction.

Reject exact, implementation-equivalent, semantically near-duplicate, or over-concentrated candidates after generation and retry only the conflicting slot without prescribing its replacement direction.
Keep all feature state leakage-safe, all new components independently ablatable, and every candidate comparable under the trusted validation protocol.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The research loop must not use validation labels as features, test labels or metrics as feedback, external training datasets, altered evaluator logic, or noncausal temporal features. A full autonomous run also requires a configured supported LLM provider or a compatible local Ollama model.
